cases.final_diagnosis: CNC-02 has a developing mechanical fault causing recurrent vibration above the 4.50 mm/s threshold, isolated to CNC-02. Vibration crossed the threshold at tick 914 (4.577 mm/s, the original alarm), again at tick 919 (4.508 mm/s, second alarm logged 4.51), and remained elevated across ticks 921-930 with clear recrossings at ticks 922 (4.574), 926 (4.510), and 928 (4.531); the mean rose from 4.318 mm/s (ticks 905-920) to 4.440 mm/s (ticks 921-930). All other running machines (CNC-04, CNC-05, CNC-06, CNC-07, CNC-08) stayed near 2.0-2.6 mm/s in the same windows, ruling out a factory-wide disturbance, and the raw readings plus the repeat alarm rule out a transient spike or nuisance trip. The specific root cause within CNC-02 (bearing, spindle, lubrication, or other mechanical cause) cannot be determined from vibration alone.

CNC-05 is not mechanically faulty. The vibration alarm (4.56 mm/s vs the 4.50 mm/s limit at tick 826) is explained by a step-up in process load, not by a developing fault. Load rose from about 54% mean (ticks 760-799, E15) to about 68% mean (ticks 800-830, E12), while vibration rose from about 3.78 mm/s mean / 4.06 mm/s max (E14) to about 4.17 mm/s mean / 4.57 mm/s max (E3, E16), crossing the limit only after the load step. Per-tick data (E17) shows vibration rising on the same ticks as the load jump (801-803). The other CNCs run at 0.9-2.19 mm/s vibration (E6-E9) but at lower loads/settings. Pre-800 vibration never approached 4.50 mm/s (max 4.06, E14), ruling out an inherently high baseline or a threshold set too low (H3), and no separate mechanical fault (H1) is indicated.

The inspection failures are concentrated in material batch 2, not in any single machine. Batch-1 jobs 7-10 all passed inspection (E5), while batch-2 jobs 11, 13 and 15 failed and jobs 12 and 14 passed — a ~60% reject rate confined to batch 2 (E5). Every failed job ran the full route through CNC-01, CNC-02, CNC-03, CNC-04, CNC-05 and CNC-06 (E6, E7, E9), so no individual CNC station is implicated, and blocking/delay does not separate failures: blocked jobs 12 (E17) and 14 (E18) passed while blocked job 11 failed (E6). This fits H1 — a defective batch-2 material lot — over H2 (blocking-induced damage, contradicted by E17/E18) and H3 (random variation, contradicted by the clean batch split in E5). Batch-3 confirmation is pending: job 16 started CNC-06 at tick 1367 (E15) but its inspection result is not yet in evidence.

All four observed batch-2 jobs (11, 12, 13, 14) failed inspection while all ten batch-1 jobs passed; this points at H1 (bad batch-2 material/lot), but machine-cause rivals H2 (a station fault, e.g. CNC-04/CNC-05 vibration step-change seen in E8/E10 starting around tick 884) and H3 (inspection station rejecting good parts) are not yet ruled out because jobs 15-18 results are still unknown and batch-1 routes after tick 884 are unobserved. CNC-04/CNC-05/CNC-06 all show elevated vibration (~1.8-2.0 mm/s mean, max ~2.6-2.8 mm/s) with CNC-04 stepping up at tick 884 (E8, E10), so a machine contribution cannot be excluded. CNC-01, CNC-02, CNC-03 sensors remain unchecked. Confidence is below the 0.90 intervene threshold, so no repair action is justified yet; none of the approved actions (bearing, setting, servo drive, hydraulics) would fix a material lot problem anyway.

Intermittent machine faults and/or multiple unrelated causes are the likely explanation for the inspection failures. While vibration levels are elevated across all machines during the relevant periods, including for job 3 which passed inspection, CNC-05 shows consistently high following errors and vibration, particularly during the time window when job 3 was processed, yet job 3 still passed. This suggests that CNC-05's issues alone cannot explain the failures.

Three batch-2 jobs (14, 19, 20) failed inspection while jobs 15–18 passed, but no machine root cause has been observed. CNC-06 blocked both job 18 (tick 1503) and job 19 (tick 1570) per E19, yet job 18 passed and job 19 failed, and CNC-06 event logs (E18) show normal start/finish durations with no error messages for jobs 14, 19 and 20. CNC-02 blocks every job after CNC-01 (E10, E13) with normal durations, and CNC-01/CNC-03/CNC-04/CNC-05 logs show nothing anomalous. Critically, no sensor readings have been checked for any machine (E3: all machines running or idle, sensors not checked), so H1 (intermittent CNC-06 CNC-05→CNC-06 handoff fault), H2 (within-batch-2 variation: material/fixture/ambient), and H3 (intermittent CNC-02 hydraulic fault) remain equally unconfirmed. The alarm names inspection failures only; it does not localize a fault, and missing sensor measurements are unknown, not normal.

CNC-01 has a likely genuine localized mechanical fault (bearing/drive strain): its vibration spiked to 7.01–7.37 mm/s, above the 4.50 mm/s alarm threshold, at ticks 521–524 (E9, E16), and while idle it ran 109–126 °F (mean ≈119 °F over ticks 480–530) against 77 °F ambient air (E5, E7), still about 116 °F at tick 540 and cooling only slowly (E18). Vibration has been normal since tick 524 (E12, E20), so the fault may be intermittent or appear only under load. The rival H2 (transient disturbance with residual heat cooling off) is not yet excluded because CNC-03's idle temperature was never measured (E13) and CNC-01's post-540 temperature trend is unknown.

CNC-03's vibration alarm (ticks 381-383, about 6.8 mm/s against a 4.50 mm/s threshold) was a one-off excursion during loaded operation, not an ongoing mechanical fault. CNC-03 was under load (load 31-35%, E6) when it alarmed, then finished job 4 at tick 392 (E15), unloaded and stopped: vibration fell to near zero (0-0.27 mm/s, ticks 393-400, E13) and CNC-03 has been idle since tick 400 (E14, E17). A single later reading at about tick 420 shows 2.23 mm/s (E19), below the alarm threshold, and no alarm has recurred. Other machines show normal vibration (CNC-01 mean 1.76 mm/s, E10; CNC-06 mean 1.82 mm/s, E11) and air temperature was stable at 75-76 °F (E7), ruling out a line-wide cause. Diagnosis H2: one-off process event while CNC-03 was cutting under load, followed by a normal stop; no underlying fault requiring repair. H1 is contradicted because CNC-03 did not stay running (E13-E17); H3 is unsupported because there has been no recurrence and CNC-03 is idle; H_factory_wide is contradicted by E7, E10, E11.

A temporary, non-recurring vibration spike on CNC-03 during ticks 71-78: readings of 5.00-5.21 mm/s exceeded the 4.50 mm/s monitoring setpoint while CNC-03 was idle with near-zero motor load (load max 4.32%, mean 0.70% over ticks 60-80). Vibration returned to normal immediately afterward (max 0.36 mm/s over ticks 80-90; max 0.21 mm/s over ticks 90-100), and CNC-04, the other idle machine checked for the same window, showed no spike (max 0.39 mm/s over ticks 71-78), so the event was localized to CNC-03, not factory-wide. Per the manual, 4.50 mm/s is a monitoring setpoint, not a confirmed failure threshold, and there is no recurrence, elevated load, temperature, or mechanical evidence. H1 (transient disturbance, no confirmed failure) is supported; H2 (developing bearing/drive fault) is contradicted by the post-alarm return to normal and by CNC-03 remaining idle, and H3 (faulty sensor) is not supported because readings normalized cleanly rather than staying erratic or biased.

CNC-04's feed-axis servo drive is wearing out. Its following error has risen through the 20 µm alarm threshold (20.26 µm at tick 1129; 18.95 µm at tick 1130; 19.59 µm at tick 1140, still climbing), while CNC-01, CNC-02, CNC-03 and CNC-05 all stay near 3-6 µm. CNC-04 power is slightly elevated (+0.59 kW over the window) while vibration and temperature are flat, matching the manual's drive-wear signature: a wearing drive adds lag only while running, draws a little more power, and leaves vibration, temperature and job times unchanged. A binding axis is unlikely (vibration and temperature are flat), and a heavier cut or faster speed is unlikely (the rise is a sustained 130-tick trend, not a step-change spike).

CNC-02 feed-axis servo drive is wearing out: its following_error has risen progressively and monotonically (bucket mean 13.792 µm at ticks 1200-1229 to 19.202 µm at ticks 1350-1360) and just crossed the 20.00 µm alarm threshold (20.103 µm at tick 1358). The fault is isolated to CNC-02: CNC-01, CNC-03, CNC-04, CNC-06 and CNC-07 all show stable following_error around 3-6 µm with no rising trend, and CNC-05 is idle. The smooth, bucket-by-bucket increase matches wear (H1), not a step parameter change (H3 expects a sudden jump when speed/cut settings changed, which E3 does not show). A servo-controller following_error channel/readout bias (H2) remains an untested rival because no independent axis-position measurement exists, so confidence is below the 0.90 level needed for an accepted intervene.

CNC-05 has a progressive hydraulic pressure loss localized to CNC-05's own hydraulic system (consistent with a leaking seal, per the manual's idle-leak signature), not a shared-supply failure. CNC-05 is idle yet its pressure fell from mean 58.959 bar (ticks 1200-1209) to mean 56.243 bar (ticks 1280-1289), with the alarm reading of 54.29 bar and another sub-setpoint reading of 54.788 bar at tick 1310 while still idle. CNC-02, the only other hydraulic station, stayed flat at roughly 68-69 bar over the same window (mean 69.027 at 1200-1209; 68.607 at 1280-1289), so the supply CNC-05 draws from is sound and the loss is confined to CNC-05. CNC-01, CNC-03, CNC-04 and CNC-06 have no hydraulics and are unaffected. Inspections have all passed, so no quality impact has appeared yet. A transducer/drift fault is a residual alternative, but continuous readings with a clear multi-tick decline and repeated actual sub-setpoint values argue against it.

CNC-02 has a genuine, progressive hydraulic pressure loss (consistent with leaking seals; a weakening pump or sticking relief valve is not yet isolated). Pressure fell from a ~63 bar mean during ticks 800-859 to ~56.8 bar at 1040-1050, tripping the 55.00 bar alarm at tick 1041, and kept falling through tick 1150 (53.05 bar) with no recovery. CNC-05 and CNC-07 — the only other stations with hydraulics — stayed flat at roughly 66-71 bar over the same windows, so this is a CNC-02 fault, not a system-wide supply issue or a transducer artifact (the trend is smooth and gapless, not erratic). Inspection pass history (jobs 7-9) shows no failures yet, but the manual warns the failure share grows as the leak grows and some jobs still pass.
